students.name: Leia

class_summary.evidence_line: 6 student evidence sets | 24 circuit items each
class_summary.evidence_analyzed: The submitted four-page Algebra 2 review circuit was scored item-by-item with partial credit for correct setup or meaningful intermediate work. Grade percentages below are teacher-review recommendations, not final grades.
strengths: The class is generally strong with factoring and algebraic structure.
Most students handled line equations, interval work, and core equation solving successfully.
Several students showed clear reasoning even when the final answer contained a small arithmetic or completion error.
needs: A repeated class pattern is stopping before every requested part or representation is complete.
Some students factor correctly but then miss a requested sum or product of factors/solutions.
Coordinate arithmetic, one-variable arithmetic, and perpendicular-line follow-through need targeted checking for a smaller group.
class_summary.highest_leverage_target: After a correct setup, use a final-answer checklist: complete every requested part, perform the requested operation, and verify arithmetic or substitution.

groupings.title: Extension / Transfer
groupings.note: Use multi-part transfer problems and require exact forms plus justification.

groupings.title: Precision / Completion
groupings.note: Keep the strong core algebra, but focus on the final requested representation, sum/product, or equation form.

groupings.title: Accuracy / Follow-Through
groupings.note: Use shorter mixed sets with explicit arithmetic and final-answer checks before moving to transfer.

class_summary.limitations: Student names were read only when the handwriting was clear enough to support a confident transcription. Two sets use stable labels because the scan did not support a reliable name reading. Scores are based only on the submitted circuit evidence and remain teacher-review recommendations.

set1.label: Interval notation
set1.teacher_move: Ask students to connect each inequality symbol to the correct bracket or parenthesis before writing the interval.
set1.discourse_move: Compare why -2 uses a bracket while 5 uses a parenthesis.

verification.method: Endpoint-inclusion check: -2 is included and 5 is excluded.

set1.label: Midpoint accuracy
set1.teacher_move: Have students average x-coordinates and y-coordinates on separate lines before simplifying.
set1.discourse_move: Explain which arithmetic step is easiest to make an error on and how you checked it.

set1.label: Solve and verify
set1.teacher_move: Ask for the least common denominator first, then require a substitution check.
set1.discourse_move: Compare clearing denominators first versus combining fractions first.

set1.label: Sum of factors
set1.prompt: Factor \(x^2-7x+12\), then give the sum of the two binomial factors.
set1.teacher_move: Separate the factorization step from the requested operation so students do not stop too early.
set1.discourse_move: State the factors first, then explain what changes when the prompt asks for their sum.

set1.label: Complete and factor
set1.prompt: Choose \(c\) so \(x^2-14x+c\) is a perfect-square trinomial, then factor it completely.
set1.teacher_move: Require both requested outputs: the value of c and the final factored form.
set1.discourse_move: Explain why half of -14 is used before squaring.

set1.label: Circle features
set1.prompt: For \((x+2)^2+(y-4)^2=36\), state the center and radius.
set1.teacher_move: Ask students to identify the sign change in the center and the square root used for radius.
set1.discourse_move: Explain why the center x-coordinate is -2 even though the equation shows +2.

verification.method: Matched standard form (x-h)^2+(y-k)^2=r^2 with h=-2, k=4, r=sqrt(36)=6.

set1.label: Perpendicular line
set1.prompt: Find an equation of the line through \((4,-1)\) perpendicular to \(3x-2y=8\).
set1.teacher_move: Have students rewrite the given line in slope-intercept form before taking the negative reciprocal.
set1.discourse_move: Justify the perpendicular slope and show how your final equation contains the given point.

verification.method: Given slope is 3/2, perpendicular slope -2/3; point-slope simplifies to 2x+3y=5 and (4,-1) satisfies it.

set1.label: Absolute value product
set1.prompt: Solve \(|3x-1|=8\), then give the product of the two solutions.
set1.teacher_move: Require both branches before allowing students to compute the product.
set1.discourse_move: Explain why an absolute-value equation creates two linear equations here.

questions.answer: They added coordinates but did not divide each sum by 2; correct midpoint \((-2,7)\).

questions.prompt: A student writes \(x^2-5x+6=(x-1)(x-6)\). Correct the factorization and explain the check.
questions.answer: \((x-2)(x-3)\); the factors multiply to 6 and add to -5.

questions.prompt: A student solves \(|2x+1|=5\) using only \(2x+1=5\). What solution is missing?
questions.answer: The second branch \(2x+1=-5\) gives the missing solution \(x=-3\).
